title: Swahili Tamarind Fish Stew
author: Chef Amina Hassan

relatedDish.note: KEN186 is an Indigenous & Tribal Dishes category version of the Swahili Tamarind Fish (KEN128). See KEN128 for the full recipe with complete heritage and cultural detail.

desc: Swahili Tamarind Fish Stew — the ancient Swahili coastal preparation of fresh fish in a tangy, sweet-sour tamarind sauce. One of the oldest and most distinctive preparations in Swahili culinary heritage. See KEN128 for the full recipe.
longDesc: Samaki wa Ukwaju represents centuries of Swahili coastal culinary tradition — fresh Indian Ocean fish combined with tamarind from Arab trade. See KEN128 for the complete recipe and heritage.
ingredients: 600g fresh fish fillets — snapper, kingfish, or barracuda
steps: Season fish with salt and turmeric.
Cook onions in oil until golden. Add garlic and ginger. Cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, curry powder, tamarind paste, brown sugar, and water. Stir well.
Simmer for 6—8 minutes until sauce thickens. Taste and balance sweet-sour.
Add fish. Spoon sauce over gently.
Cover and simmer 8—12 minutes until cooked through.
chefTips: Taste and adjust the tamarind-sugar balance before adding fish.
See KEN128 for the full technique and cultural notes.

healthBenefits: Tamarind provides iron and B vitamins.
